authors: Nasrin Sadeghianpourhamami; Johannes Deleu; Chris Develder
problem: Joint coordination of a set of EV charging stations for load flattening (demand response)
method: Batch RL: fitted Q-iteration on a new MDP whose state bins EVs by time-to-departure and remaining charging time
architecture: MLP Q-function (128-64 ReLU) over a binned 2-D grid state independent of number of stations; fractional action per bin
environment_or_data: ElaadNL public charging transactions (busiest 10 and 50 stations, 2015)
baselines: Business-as-usual; perfect-knowledge quadratic-optimisation oracle
key_results: Cost reduction vs BAU 39% (10 stations) and 30.4% (50 stations); learned policy 13% / 15.6% above oracle cost; policy trained on 10 stations tested with up to 10x scaled arrivals (largest jump at 2x)
limitations: Unfinished-charging only penalised (large M), no violation statistics; no transformer limit; same charging rate assumed for all EVs; discrete binning
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1809.10679v2 (arXiv version of the TSG paper)

authors: Zachary J. Lee; George Lee; Ted Lee; Cheng Jin; Rand Lee; Zhi Low; Daniel Chang; Christine Ortega; Steven H. Low
problem: Real-world large-scale workplace smart charging (Caltech ACN) under congested infrastructure
method: Adaptive Scheduling Algorithm: convex optimisation solved in MPC fashion (re-solve on events or every 5 min)
constraint_handling: other:hard infrastructure constraints in convex program + energy as <= constraint with non-completion penalty
environment_or_data: Caltech ACN (54 EVSEs on one transformer, 10,415 sessions May-Oct 2018); ACN-Sim
baselines: Uncontrolled, round robin, LLF, EDF; offline optimal with perfect information
key_results: Profit ~3.4x uncontrolled; 98.1% of offline optimum in idealised setting and ~90% with non-ideal batteries/EVSEs; up to 14.1% more energy than EDF at 30 kW transformer capacity
limitations: Energy delivery best-effort (<=), not guaranteed; requires per-step optimisation; unbalanced three-phase handled via SOC or conservative affine constraints

authors: Tongxin Li; Bo Sun; Yue Chen; Zixin Ye; Steven H. Low; Adam Wierman
problem: Real-time aggregator-operator coordination of EV charging with privacy of load constraints
method: Maximum entropy feedback (MEF) learned with SAC; penalized predictive control (PPC) at operator
architecture: MLP actor-critic (SAC) producing a probability vector over discrete aggregate power levels
constraint_handling: penalty+other:LLF dispatch for per-EV rate/arrival constraints
environment_or_data: Caltech ACN-Data (54 chargers, 150 kW, 12-min slots); CAISO prices
baselines: Vanilla MPC with full state; offline optimal
key_results: Theorem: PPC with exact MEF reproduces offline optimum under strict convexity/log-concavity; learned MEF gives 'almost' feasible results; PPC cost below MPC in plots (no percentage reported)
limitations: Guarantee only for exact MEF and continuous scalar action; learned MEF uses reward penalties; experiments use discrete levels

authors: Hepeng Li; Zhiqiang Wan; Haibo He
problem: Single-EV charging/discharging under random arrival/departure and prices with full-charge requirement
method: Constrained MDP solved with model-free safe DRL (constrained policy optimisation style)
architecture: Deep neural network policy (details not read)
environment_or_data: Real-world electricity prices (details not read)
baselines: Not read (abstract only)
key_results: Abstract claims cost reduction while ensuring full charge without manual penalty tuning; numbers not read
limitations: Single EV; constraint satisfied in expectation (CMDP) per abstract wording, not hard

authors: Oliver Frendo; Nadine Gaertner; Heiner Stuckenschmidt
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
problem: Workplace smart charging with limited supply; uncertain EV departure times
method: Regression models trained on historical sessions predict departure; predictions fed into a prioritising smart-charging heuristic
environment_or_data: Historical workplace charging data (details not read)
baselines: Heuristic without departure prediction
key_results: More accurate departure predictions improve prioritisation and fair share (qualitative)

authors: Niangjun Chen; Christian Kurniawan; Yorie Nakahira; Lijun Chen; Steven H. Low
problem: Online adaptive EV charging as feasibility problem (energy by deadline, rate limits, station power limit)
method: Smoothed least-laxity-first (sLLF): maximise concave sum of next-slot laxities; closed-form clipped water-filling with common level found by bisection
environment_or_data: ACN Caltech CAGarage, Google Mountain View and Sunnyvale traces (52,362 sessions, 104 locations)
baselines: EDF, LLF, equal share, remaining-energy-proportional, online LP; offline LP for min feasible power
key_results: Rate r_i = clip(rbar_i(L - laxity_i + 1), 0, min(rbar_i, e_i)); 100% feasibility with only 7% power augmentation (EDF 139%, OLP 28%); theorems on power(+rate) augmentation
limitations: Online feasibility not guaranteed without augmentation; known departure and energy assumed; no prices/profit objective

authors: Liangliang Hao; Jiangliang Jin; Yunjian Xu
problem: Joint online pricing and charging scheduling for a public charging station (profit or welfare)
method: Laxity-differentiated pricing + deadline-differentiated threshold charging policy embedded in SAC to reduce action dimension
environment_or_data: Stochastic prices and renewable generation (details not read)
baselines: Alternative pricing and charging schemes (details not read)
key_results: Threshold policy shown optimal under arbitrary dynamics (per abstract); SAC+LDP+DTC outperforms alternatives
limitations: Abstract only; constraint enforcement details not read

authors: Vladimir Dyo
problem: Domestic EV charging peak reduction without predicting plug-in duration
method: Boost-then-low-power policy whose two parameters are tuned by retrospective RL-style search on past sessions
environment_or_data: UK dataset: ~3.17M sessions, 22,731 domestic charge points
baselines: Uncontrolled; hypothetical oracle with known duration
key_results: Linear regression of session duration MAPE ~414%; 31% aggregate evening-peak reduction (history 30); energy deficit 1.4-5.0% depending on history
limitations: Energy deficit not eliminated; single charger per policy; reward set to -inf above 10 kWh loss

authors: Christos D. Korkas; Christos D. Tsaknakis; Athanasios Ch. Kapoutsis; Elias Kosmatopoulos
problem: Station with N charging spots, PV and V2G: cost minimisation and user satisfaction
method: Distributed MARL: one DDPG agent per charging spot trained with difference rewards from a coordinator
architecture: Per-spot MLP DDPG actor/critic with fixed 10-value local observation
environment_or_data: Chargym environment; four price profiles incl. NordPool; typical PV day; 10/20/35/50 spots
baselines: Rule-based controllers; centralised DDPG and SAC
key_results: Up to 25% energy-cost reduction and up to 20% user-satisfaction improvement (abstract); local observation size constant across station sizes
limitations: Departure SoC only penalised; no aggregate transformer cap in model; weight sharing/transfer across sizes not stated
evidence_source: https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/17/15/3694 (HTML, partial; results section not reached)

authors: Emily van Huffelen; Roel Brouwer; Marjan van den Akker
problem: Online scheduling of EV charging in parking-lot network under cable capacities; minimise tardiness
method: Online serial/parallel schedule generation schemes with priority rules (FCFS, EDD, ELSTu) and destroy-and-repair

baselines: Uncontrolled 9 kW; FCFS; EDD; variants
key_results: Eliminates cable overload (60-70% of time uncontrolled); avg delay ~95 s, 1.6% EVs delayed with 15-min rescheduling
limitations: Energy always delivered but departure may be delayed; no prices/V2G

authors: Koen Ponse; Felix Kleuker; Aske Plaat; Thomas M. Moerland
problem: JAX-accelerated charging-station environment for RL
method: PPO (PureJaxRL) on configurable station tree
architecture: MLP PPO; observation concatenates per-EVSE states
environment_or_data: Configurable station (16 chargers in main tests); NL/FR/DE prices; Poisson arrivals; user profiles
baselines: Max-rate rule; speed comparisons vs EV2Gym, Chargym, SustainGym
key_results: Architecture limits enforced by rescaling currents; unmet demand penalised; 17-2820x speedups depending on setting
limitations: Isolated network; no shared transformer; observation grows with chargers

authors: Cesar Diaz-Londono; Stavros Orfanoudakis; Pedro P. Vergara; Peter Palensky; Fredy Ruiz; Giambattista Gruosso
problem: MPC for G2V/V2G demand response at a charge point operator
method: Economic MPC and optimal-flexibility MPC (LP for G2V, MILP for V2G) integrated with EV2Gym
constraint_handling: other:hard constraints in MPC (departure SoC bound, transformer limit)
environment_or_data: EV2Gym residential scenarios; 10 EVSEs/~25 EVs main case; up to 60 EVSEs for timing
baselines: Charge-as-fast-as-possible; MPC variants against each other
key_results: eMPC V2G profit 50.8 EUR vs AFAP -47.6 EUR (50 runs); per-step time <1.5% of step at 60 EVSEs
limitations: No perfect-information optimum benchmark; assumes known EV schedules; degradation increases with V2G
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.11963 (preprint version, same authors; published EPSR version not read)
